subject: Segfault using HMC and is AD fixing model's constants

messages.author: b15b7599f50d0b5d
messages.subject: Segfault using HMC and is AD fixing model's constants
parts:
I need to use HMC as a sampler because of the complexity of the posterior distribution of my model, but I run into a segfault when running the HMC model. Since I'm new to nimble, I have no idea where to look.

My code is relatively long to go through, but here is the gist of it:
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
code <- nimbleCode({
    for (i in seq(1, n - 1)) {
        for (j in seq(i + 1, n)) {
            p[i, j] <- 1 / (1 + (angular_distance(theta[i], theta[j], b, pi_)
                               * radius_div_mu / kappa[i] / kappa[j])^beta)
            adjacency[i, j] ~ dbern(p[i, j])
        }
    }
    for (i in 1:n) {
        theta[i] ~ dunif(-pi_, pi_)
        kappa[i] ~ dunif(kappa_min, kappa_max)
    }
})

model <- nimbleModel(
    model_code,
    constants = list(n = n, beta = beta, radius_div_mu = radius_div_mu,
                     kappa_min = kappa_min, kappa_max = kappa_max,
                     gamma = gamma, b = b, pi_ = pi),
    data = list(adjacency = adjacency),
    inits = list(theta = theta, kappa = kappa),
    buildDerivs = TRUE
)

hmc <- buildHMC(model)
compiled_model <- compileNimble(model)
compiled_hmc <- compileNimble(hmc, project = model)
samples <- runMCMC(compiled_hmc, nchain = chains, niter = 1000, nburnin = 500)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Which returns:

 *** caught segfault ***
address 0xYZ, cause 'memory not mapped'

I omitted my function definitions and values of the parameters, but I can add some more details if debugging is needed.

The "adjacency" matrix is symmetric and so I only iterate on the lower half of it. I think the rest of the matrix is not initialized because of this. Is the HMC function trying to compute the jacobian matrix for the whole matrix and is the reason behind the segfault?

I also have a second question regarding HMC which is unrelated. I define my own nimble functions perform calculations in my model. Since these functions receive in argument constants of the model, I'm wondering if using "buildDerivs=TRUE" automatically ignores their gradient evaluation. If that is not the case, I cannot make it work and I'll post another question.

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: Segfault using HMC and is AD fixing model's constants
parts:
Thanks for using nimbleHMC, and also sending your question.

A very short answer would be: it's not apparent offhand what's going wrong, and to really figure it out, we'd need a reproducible example.  If you'd prefer to send that (model code, data, etc) off-list, then that's no problem at all.

No, only populating half of the values in the adjacency matrix is not a problem.  The HMC sampler will only access and use the values in the parts you access inside the for-loops.

That said: you said that you "only iterate on the lower half of it.... the rest of the matrix is not initialized because of this", but a quick inspection of the for-loops in your code makes it appear like (instead) you only iterate on the upper half of it.  So, perhaps there's something going wrong here (providing values for the wrong half of the adjacency matrix), that might be causing this problem.  It might be worth a look at that.

Regarding your second question: If by "ignores their gradient evaluation" you mean "ignores the gradient evaluation of the custom-written nimble functions entirely", then no, gradients of these functions are not ignored, but rather algebraically derived (via automatic differentiation), while using the values of the constant arguments you provided.  Or, if by "ignores their gradient evaluation", you mean the "ignores the partial derivatives of the custom-written nimble functions w.r.t. the constant-valued arguments", then yes, automatic differentiation is not applied to the constant-valued arguments, much the same as it would not be applied to an argument which is hard-coded as a number (say, 5).  The gradient (partial derivatives) of the function are only calculated w.r.t. continuous-valued non-constant arguments, as is necessary for HMC sampling.

Cheers, keep at it,
Daniel

Sorry to resurrect this old thread. I had the same problem with a segfault when using nimbleHMC and calling runMCMC, even when running the HMC example in the manual (https://r-nimble.org/html_manual/cha-mcmc.html#subsec:HMC-example). I'm using Ubuntu 22.04, nimble 1.1.0 and nimbleHMC 0.2.1. 

The source of the problem for me seems to be the compiler I was using. I had the compiler manually set to clang/clang++ 14 in ~/.R/Makevars. When I removed these settings (implicitly telling R to use gcc/g++ instead), everything worked.

Ken

Le mardi 28 mars 2023 à 09:46:07 UTC-4, Daniel Turek a écrit :
Thanks for using nimbleHMC, and also sending your question.

A very short answer would be: it's not apparent offhand what's going wrong, and to really figure it out, we'd need a reproducible example.  If you'd prefer to send that (model code, data, etc) off-list, then that's no problem at all.

No, only populating half of the values in the adjacency matrix is not a problem.  The HMC sampler will only access and use the values in the parts you access inside the for-loops.

That said: you said that you "only iterate on the lower half of it.... the rest of the matrix is not initialized because of this", but a quick inspection of the for-loops in your code makes it appear like (instead) you only iterate on the upper half of it.  So, perhaps there's something going wrong here (providing values for the wrong half of the adjacency matrix), that might be causing this problem.  It might be worth a look at that.

Regarding your second question: If by "ignores their gradient evaluation" you mean "ignores the gradient evaluation of the custom-written nimble functions entirely", then no, gradients of these functions are not ignored, but rather algebraically derived (via automatic differentiation), while using the values of the constant arguments you provided.  Or, if by "ignores their gradient evaluation", you mean the "ignores the partial derivatives of the custom-written nimble functions w.r.t. the constant-valued arguments", then yes, automatic differentiation is not applied to the constant-valued arguments, much the same as it would not be applied to an argument which is hard-coded as a number (say, 5).  The gradient (partial derivatives) of the function are only calculated w.r.t. continuous-valued non-constant arguments, as is necessary for HMC sampling.

Cheers, keep at it,
Daniel

Le mardi 28 mars 2023 à 09:46:07 UTC-4, Daniel Turek a écrit :
Thanks for using nimbleHMC, and also sending your question.

A very short answer would be: it's not apparent offhand what's going wrong, and to really figure it out, we'd need a reproducible example.  If you'd prefer to send that (model code, data, etc) off-list, then that's no problem at all.

No, only populating half of the values in the adjacency matrix is not a problem.  The HMC sampler will only access and use the values in the parts you access inside the for-loops.

That said: you said that you "only iterate on the lower half of it.... the rest of the matrix is not initialized because of this", but a quick inspection of the for-loops in your code makes it appear like (instead) you only iterate on the upper half of it.  So, perhaps there's something going wrong here (providing values for the wrong half of the adjacency matrix), that might be causing this problem.  It might be worth a look at that.

Regarding your second question: If by "ignores their gradient evaluation" you mean "ignores the gradient evaluation of the custom-written nimble functions entirely", then no, gradients of these functions are not ignored, but rather algebraically derived (via automatic differentiation), while using the values of the constant arguments you provided.  Or, if by "ignores their gradient evaluation", you mean the "ignores the partial derivatives of the custom-written nimble functions w.r.t. the constant-valued arguments", then yes, automatic differentiation is not applied to the constant-valued arguments, much the same as it would not be applied to an argument which is hard-coded as a number (say, 5).  The gradient (partial derivatives) of the function are only calculated w.r.t. continuous-valued non-constant arguments, as is necessary for HMC sampling.

Cheers, keep at it,
Daniel
